headline: High risk: Cline’s default workspace/file and browser tooling can ingest or act on content from a non-isolated shared workspace, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure; awesome-nlp adds no blocking controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads workspace files, uses MCP, and runs browsers, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or web pages can be treated as instructions. awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only repo, so it does not block that pathway. The interaction is inferred from Cline’s documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is placed in a workspace file that Cline reads
IF Cline is connected to an MCP server or browser page containing untrusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict Cline to a clean workspace with no untrusted files
Disable or remove MCP servers for the session
Use a separate review-only workspace for imported content
Require manual approval for any action derived from file or browser text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad network egress, reads workspace files, and handles model-provider API keys, so sensitive content in the workspace can be uploaded to third parties during normal operation. awesome-nlp is docs-only and does not add a protective boundary. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through Cline’s inference and browser/tooling stack.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the VS Code workspace
IF Cline sends workspace context to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets and sensitive documents from the workspace
Use a throwaway API key with minimal scope
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed
Run Cline in a separate workspace with least-privilege files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via the workspace filesystem across instances. awesome-nlp is not runnable, so it does not itself write, but the pair still conflicts when Cline operates in a workspace containing shared files or git state. Uncertainty favors medium because the write surface is explicit and shared-state coordination is absent by default.
conditions: IF two Cline instances or other tools touch the same workspace directory
IF git state is modified without external locking
mitigations: Use one writer per workspace
Pause other agents before edits
Commit or stash before starting Cline
Place the pair in separate directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on workspace content and browser output, so if it treats upstream text as authoritative it may propagate errors into edits or tool actions. awesome-nlp provides no verification layer because it is a docs-only list. The pathway exists in default Cline workflows, but the blast radius is usually bounded to workspace changes rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF Cline uses generated text from files or browser pages as the basis for edits
IF no human verification step is inserted before tool actions
mitigations: Require a human review step before commits
Ask Cline to cite source lines before acting
Limit tasks to read-only analysis first
Separate fact-gathering from execution in different sessions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, and Cline’s profile only shows generic workspace/browser handling plus model-provider keys. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not specifically documented, the risk is limited to ordinary policy mismatch if the operator places regulated data into Cline’s workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the workspace
IF the configured model provider or MCP server has incompatible residency or retention terms
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Verify provider residency and retention settings
Use a local or approved provider for sensitive tasks
Document a data-handling policy before use
